title: A Spacecraft Visits a Crashed Asteroid
summary:
A spacecraft has come to an asteroid to look at the damage from a big space crash. The first close-up photos will come out later on Wednesday.

Four years ago, NASA's Dart spacecraft crashed into the asteroid Dimorphos on purpose. It was flying at 22,000 kilometres per hour, about 14,000 miles per hour. The crash broke the spacecraft. Now a spacecraft from Europe, called Hera, is looking at the crash site to see what happened.

Dimorphos is about 150 metres wide. It goes around a bigger asteroid called Didymos. The asteroid is not a danger to Earth. This was the first test to see if we can push an asteroid away if one ever comes toward Earth.

The crash did change the asteroid's path. Before the crash, Dimorphos took 11 hours and 55 minutes to go around Didymos. After the crash, it took about 33 minutes less. The crash was so big that a trail of broken pieces about 10,000 kilometres long was seen by telescopes.
why_it_matters: One day, knowing how to move an asteroid could help protect Earth, and this test shows it might work.
